name: Eyebrow pencil / powder

card.summary: Pencils and powders that fill sparse or uneven brows with pigment; a daily-wear cosmetic with essentially no published research behind it.
card.aka: Brow pencil, brow powder, brow filler
card.note: Cosmetic cover only; it does not change hair growth.

quick.overview:
Eyebrow pencils and powders are makeup products used to outline, darken or fill in the brows. Pencils draw fine hair-like strokes, while powders (often applied with a small angled brush) give a softer, fuller finish.
In looksmaxxing and grooming discussions they are a way to change brow density or shape without surgery or transplants. Little published research exists on these products themselves, so what is known comes mainly from general descriptions of eyebrow cosmetics.
quick.mechanism: The products deposit pigment on the skin and hairs, filling gaps and sharpening the outline. Powders are usually matched closely to natural hair colour for a softer look [1]. They affect appearance only while worn and do not alter hair growth.
quick.risks: As ordinary cosmetics they carry the usual risk of skin irritation or allergy to ingredients in some individuals. No studies exist on adverse effects specific to brow pencils or powders.

chain: Pigment is deposited on skin and hairs
Gaps and edges in the brow are filled and defined
Fuller, more symmetrical brows frame the eyes
angle.text: Pencils and powders immediately fill sparse or uneven brow areas and sharpen the outline, giving a denser, more defined brow for as long as the makeup stays on. Users choose them to adjust shape and fullness without a procedure.

lead: Eyebrow pencils and powders are makeup products that outline the brows or fill sparse patches with pigment, so the brows look fuller, more even and more defined. Pencils and shaders can draw fine strokes that imitate individual hairs, brow gels add texture so hairs look thicker, and powders or matte eyeshadows in a shade close to natural hair colour give a softer, filled-in finish [1]. The effect is immediate and lasts while the product is worn.

People use them to change brow density, shape and symmetry without surgery or transplants, and to frame the eyes. A review of eyebrows in facial expression and recognition reports that the eye region carries most of the information used to read emotion and that eyebrows are at least as influential as the eyes for recognising a face, which is one reason brow shape and fill change how a whole face reads.[9] A 2022 PLoS One study in which 200 raters judged photographs of 20 men with and without subtle professional makeup found that the made-up faces were rated as more attractive by both male and female raters.[4]

Brow styling has changed with fashion over the centuries, from hikimayu in 8th-century Japan to the thin pencilled brows of the 1920s and 1930s.[1] A 2023 literature review of 43 papers published between 2000 and 2022 concluded that eyebrow makeup meaningfully affects appearance and noted that mask-wearing during the pandemic shifted attention toward eye and brow makeup.[5]

Brow makeup sits alongside other options for sparse or uneven brows, including tinting, microblading and follicle transplants, and it is the one that needs no procedure and can be changed daily as fashion and personal taste shift.[1] Wikipedia notes that stigma against men wearing makeup has weakened, particularly in the United States, and that more men use cosmetics in the 21st century, which is the setting in which brow pencils, gels and powders are discussed in grooming forums.[8][7]
infobox: Pencils, shaders, powders, gels, brow brushes [1]

paras: Brushes, shaders and pencils are used to define the brow or make it look fuller; brow gels add texture, and powders or eyeshadows matched to natural colour give a softer finish [1]. Eye pencils generally come in powder-based and wax-based forms; wax-based pencils are described as the cheapest and most common eyeliner type and contain roughly half wax, with pigments such as black iron oxides and titanium dioxide [3].

Brow pencils range from fine-tipped retractable pencils to firmer shaders and are used in short flicks that follow the direction of hair growth to imitate individual hairs; powders are applied with a small angled brush for a softer, shadowed fill, and gels set the result.[1] Wikipedia advises shades closest to natural hair colour, and notes that permanent dye is a separate method of darkening brows.[1]

Sparse areas can result from over-plucking, genetics or age-related thinning. Wikipedia lists powders and microblading as ways of imitating hairs in those areas, and brow transplants, which move follicles from the back of the scalp, for people with genetically thin or over-plucked brows.[1] Pencils and powders are temporary: they wear off and do not change hair growth.

Clinicians who write on loss of eyebrows and eyelashes (madarosis) describe both the functional and psychological impact of missing brows and cover management options for its common causes; a 2023 practical guide in Dermatology and Therapy is one such review.[9]

sections.h: Why brows matter to the face
paras: Wikipedia reports that eyebrows are thought to have evolved mainly for communication, since their movement conveys subtle emotions, citing a 2018 Nature Ecology and Evolution study by Godinho, Spikins and O'Higgins.[1] A 2021 review in the Journal of Craniofacial Surgery by Hwang describes the eye region as the most important for reading emotion and eyebrows as at least as influential as the eyes for recognition, and reports the most preferred brow archetype was the so-called Anastasia type, with the lateral end of the brow placed about two-thirds of the way along the eye from the outer corner.[9]

A 2023 Vision Research experiment by Skog and colleagues showed participants faces in visual noise, with and without eyebrows, and found the eye region was most informative for detecting surprise; the eye effect was stronger without eyebrows and participants did not infer missing brows.[9] These studies concern natural brows rather than cosmetics, but they describe the features that pencils and powders are used to adjust.

Brow products change how dense, arched and symmetrical the brows look. In a 2019 Frontiers in Psychology study, researchers used machine learning on 300 images of East Asian women to relate eye, eyebrow and face shape to rated attractiveness and suggested the results could inform makeup and beauty practice.[6]

The 2022 PLoS One experiment on subtle makeup in male faces, which used professionally applied makeup and 200 raters, found higher attractiveness ratings for the made-up faces.[4] That study covered makeup as a whole rather than brow products alone.

Wikipedia reports that in 8th-century Japan hikimayu involved removing the natural brows and painting or pencilling them in higher up, that some high-status women in Elizabethan England removed their brows, and that thin, plucked brows were fashionable in the 1920s and 1930s, a look associated with Joan Crawford.[1] It adds that shaved brow lines were popular among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s.[1]

Dark eye lining has a long history: kohl-lined eyes appear in the tomb of Nakht in Thebes, dated to the 15th century BC, and wax-based pencils are now the most common eyeliner form.[3] Wikipedia's article on cosmetics says they have been used for thousands of years, with ancient Egyptians and Sumerians among early users, and that firms such as Elizabeth Arden, Helena Rubinstein, Max Factor, Revlon and Estee Lauder shaped the modern industry.[8]

Wikipedia's cosmetics article says the US FDA oversees cosmetics but that products and most ingredients do not need approval before sale, with color additives the exception, while in the European Union Regulation EC 1223/2009 governs cosmetics, requires ingredient labelling and a named responsible person.[8] It reports that fragrances and preservatives are common causes of allergic contact dermatitis.[8]

Pencils and powders sit on the skin surface and wash off. Semi-permanent alternatives have their own literature: a 2025 narrative review in Skin Appendage Disorders describes rising demand for microblading together with reported dissatisfaction, complications and immune-mediated adverse events, and 2024 case reports describe sarcoidosis presenting in microbladed brows in several patients, though the authors say a causal link is not established.[9] No studies specific to adverse effects of brow pencils or powders were located.

Other approaches to brow appearance include tweezing, waxing and threading; cosmetic tattooing or microblading, described as a 21st-century practice that implants pigment in small cuts; transplants of follicles; and surgical brow lifts, described in 1919 by Raymond Passot [1]. These are covered in separate entries. Microblading, which Wikipedia says became popular in the 21st century, implants pigment in small cuts to mimic hairs and lasts far longer than pencil or powder.[1][9]

Brow fashion has swung between thick and thin: Audrey Hepburn is remembered for thick brows, Joan Crawford for pencil-thin 1930s brows, and shaved brow lines were popular with some young people in the 1990s and 2000s [1]. Wikipedia notes that Western men reportedly pluck their brows more than before, though it gives no source for the trend [1].
The 2023 review of eyebrow makeup trends reports that mask-wearing during the pandemic moved attention toward the eyes and brows and so toward brow products [5].

No studies found on brow pencils or powders themselves. Related research on makeup and attractiveness, on eyebrow makeup trends, and on the role of eyebrows in expression and recognition is summarised above.[4][5][6][9]

timeline.event: Kohl-lined eyes appear in the tomb of Nakht in Thebes [3].
Hikimayu in Japan: natural brows are removed and painted or pencilled in higher [1].
Raymond Passot describes a surgical eyebrow lift [1].
Thin, plucked and pencilled brows are fashionable [1].
Doctors begin using Botox to temporarily raise the brows [1].
Shaved brow lines become popular among some young people [1].
Frontiers in Psychology study relates eye, brow and face shape to rated attractiveness in 300 images [6].
PLoS One study finds subtle makeup raises rated attractiveness of male faces [4].
Review of 43 papers describes post-COVID shift toward eye and brow makeup [5].
Narrative review of microblading describes demand alongside complications [9].

lore.intro: Brow pencils and powders come up in grooming forums mostly in passing, as a quick way to restyle brows or cover sparse patches.[7]

claims.claim: Pencilled-in brows can stand in for natural ones
claims.believers: A T Nation member describes years of drawn-in brows and half brows where only stubs were kept and the rest pencilled [7].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes brow pencils, shaders and powders as standard ways to fill sparse areas, and notes hikimayu in 8th-century Japan involved painting brows on [1].

claims.claim: Makeup makes faces look more attractive
claims.believers: Grooming communities treat subtle cosmetics as a fast, reversible way to improve how the face reads.
claims.experts: A 2022 PLoS One study of 200 raters found subtle professional makeup raised attractiveness ratings of male faces; it tested makeup as a whole, not brow products alone [4].

claims.claim: Brow powder or pencil makes brows grow back
claims.believers: Some shoppers hope sparse brows will recover with products.
claims.experts: These products deposit pigment and do not alter hair growth; hair-growth options such as transplants are separate procedures [1].

claims.claim: Brow shape and fill change how the eyes and whole face read
claims.believers: Grooming communities treat brows as a frame for the eyes and a quick lever on facial impression.[7]
claims.experts: A review in the Journal of Craniofacial Surgery reports eyebrows are at least as influential as the eyes for face recognition and describes preferred brow archetypes; experiments on missing brows show the eye region carries most expression information.[9]

claims.claim: Pencilled brows are a safer alternative to microblading or tattooing
claims.believers: Some users prefer removable makeup because it can be changed daily and carries no procedure.[7]
claims.experts: Reviews of microblading describe complications and immune-mediated reactions in some patients; no studies specific to pencil or powder adverse effects were located.[9]

claims.claim: Men can wear brow makeup unnoticed
claims.believers: Users say a shade close to natural colour gives a fuller brow that reads as natural.[1]
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes stigma around male makeup has eased, particularly in the United States; no study has tested how often brow makeup is detected.[8]
